fields.study_design: systematic-style literature review of academic and grey literature on water poverty in England and Wales, 1985-2022, synthesised as a chronological narrative around policy milestones (SPIDER search framework, PRISMA-style flow, no formal quality appraisal)
fields.sample_size: four academic databases and 35 grey sources (water company, regulator, consumer-body and NGO websites); search strings combining water consumers, affordability or vulnerability terms and England or Wales (Table 2); titles and abstracts screened against inclusion criteria (full text for grey documents without abstracts); the number of included documents is in the PRISMA flow diagram (Figure 1), which was not captured in the converted text; no meta-analysis
fields.effect_measure: chronological narrative synthesis around the 1999 Water Industry Act, the 2008 Walker Review and the 2021 CCW Affordability Review; no pooled estimate; no formal quality appraisal (influence rather than quality was used for grey literature)
fields.section: Full text (20 pages, Water Policy 25(5):492-511): Introduction; Methods (SPIDER, Tables 1-2, PRISMA Figure 1, quality appraisal); narrative sections on 1985-1999, 1999-2008, 2008-2021 and the present; Discussion; Limitations
fields.exact_location: Methods (literature compilation and quality appraisal paragraphs, Table 1 SPIDER, Table 2 search terms); Limitations paragraph (grey databases not searchable with strings); Water Policy 25(5):492-511

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a systematic-style review of academic and grey literature on water poverty in England and Wales, synthesised as a policy-history narrative; read in full text 2026-10-04. Prevalence figures quoted from regulators (about 18-20% of households above 3% of income, 5-10% above 5%).
pdf_note: Water Policy 25(5):492-511, English, 20 pages (iwaponline repository PDF) read in the methods, narrative and limitation sections
notes: TOOL FLAG: the paper describes a systematic-style review (SPIDER framework, PRISMA flow diagram, 4 academic databases and 35 grey sources), so it could be treated as a hybrid review like S329 and appraised with AMSTAR 2 (expected Critically Low: no protocol, no excluded-study list, no appraisal); it is currently under the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework. Decision for the researcher.
